subject: Re: Azure private plan — billing cadence & co-sell split
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@heliohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private plan — billing cadence & co-sell split

Naomi,

Thanks for the call earlier. Before we move to legal, procurement has a few open items we need written confirmation on for the Azure private plan:

- Billing cadence: can Redwood support monthly usage billing through the marketplace merchant flow, or do you require an annual committed SKU for private plans? If annual, can we do staged invoicing (50% upfront / 50% on go-live)?
- Marketplace & co-sell split: what % is Redwood expecting as the default for co-sell revenue share? Please confirm whether the split is applied before or after marketplace fees.
- Tax & MRC handling for Azure private offers — who is merchant of record and how will tax invoices be issued?
- Security/compliance: procurement requested SOC 2 type II report and certificate; I attached our procurement checklist (Procurement_DueDiligence.pdf).

We have a target internal approval window of 2 weeks, so quick alignment on the above will help. Copying Arjun (legal) on next thread.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
VP Procurement
HelioHealth

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — billing cadence & co-sell split

Elena — thanks, great to pick this up in writing. Quick answers and suggested next steps below.

- Billing cadence: we support both models. For Private Plans on Azure you can choose an annual committed SKU (recommended for committed consumption & reserved pricing) or monthly usage billing. If you select annual, we commonly support staged invoice schedules (example: 50% initial + 50% on go-live). Monthly usage billing runs through the marketplace merchant flow and is invoiced monthly by the marketplace (Azure), unless you want Redwood to invoice directly via a partner agreement — that requires a different commercial path.

- Co-sell split: standard practice is to calculate partner splits on the net revenue post-marketplace fees. Our typical commercial starting point for co-sell is 70/30 in favor of the selling partner for strategic accounts, but that is negotiable based on commit, GTM investment, and support footprint.

- Merchant of record: for Azure private offers, Azure generally acts as merchant-of-record for the marketplace transaction. Tax invoices and VAT handling follow Azure policies; if you need Redwood to be MPR (merchant) we can explore that but it usually requires separate contracting and billing changes.

- Security: SOC 2 Type II report is available; attaching our mutual action plan template (HelioHealth_MAAP_v1.xlsx) to capture procurement/legal asks and timelines.

Next steps: Ben (CC) will draft redlines that reflect a staged invoice option and a proposed 65/35 split with a short-term holdback clause for the first 90 days. If that sounds reasonable, we can circulate redlines and get legal on a short review.

I can host a 30-min commercial call Friday to run through the commercial exhibit if helpful.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@heliohealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed commercial redlines (payment cadence & split)

Elena / Arjun — attaching our proposed redlines for the Azure Private Plan commercial exhibit (Redwood_Redlines_v1.docx). Key points called out in the redline:

1) Payment schedule: 50% due within 30 days of countersign, remaining 50% due within 30 days of production go-live. For monthly usage path: billing via Azure marketplace, net-30.
2) Revenue split: propose 65/35 split to HelioHealth for the first 12 months, moving to 70/30 after 12 months contingent on >$X M ARR. Split is calculated after Azure marketplace fees and taxes.
3) Audit & holdback: Helio requested an initial 90-day reconciliation holdback; proposed alternative is a 30-day settlement holdback limited to usage reconciliation disputes rather than an open escrow.
4) Term & termination: standard 12-month term with 60 days notice for cancellation for mutual convenience.

If you need extended payment terms (net-60), we will need executive approval; please confirm intent and we will loop legal.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Redlines_v1.docx

From: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@heliohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@heliohealth.com>, External Counsel <counsel@heliohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed commercial redlines (payment cadence & split)

Naomi / Ben — attaching HelioHealth's redlines (Helio_Redlines_Azure_PrivatePlan.pdf). From legal/procurement perspective the key asks are:

- Payment terms: Helio requests net-60 for the initial year given budget cycles; if Redwood requires 50% upfront we can do 30% upfront + 70% net-60.
- Holdback: legal insists on a 90-day reconciliation holdback for first-year usage to allow our billing team to validate marketplace metering; please propose an escrow or alternative guarantee.
- Revenue split: Helio wants clarity that splits will be applied gross of certain pass-through credits and that Marketplace fees are excluded from the split calculation — we propose a 60/40 split in Helio's favor for the first 12 months.
- Audit & records: request quarterly usage/export access and a one-time audit right within 12 months.

We are prepared to move quickly but need Redwood's legal to sign off on holdback mechanics and to confirm whether Redwood will accept net-60.

Thanks,
Arjun Patel
Sr. Counsel & Procurement
HelioHealth

Attachment: Helio_Redlines_Azure_PrivatePlan.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@heliohealth.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@heliohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: HelioHealth asks for net-60 + 90-day holdback — approval request

Team — looping in legal and partnerships leadership. Helio is pushing net-60 and a 90-day reconciliation holdback for the first year. They also want a 60/40 split in their favor for 12 months. Summary of options we discussed:

Option A (commercial compromise): 30% upfront, 70% net-45; 30-day reconciliation holdback (no escrow), 65/35 split for 12 months -> move to 70/30 thereafter.
Option B (more conservative): 50% upfront, 50% on go-live; no long-term holdback, 65/35 split; require net-30 for remaining balances.
Option C (accept ask): 30% upfront, 70% net-60; 90-day escrow/holdback; 60/40 split for 12 months. Executive approval required for C.

Impacts to call out:
- Cashflow: Option C delays ~40% of expected cash beyond normal collection windows and increases ARR ramp risk.
- Marketplace complexity: escrow/holdback mechanics require coordination with Azure marketplace merchant policies and may introduce extra ops work for reconciliation.
- Competitive risk: Helio has strong leverage on product integration and co-sell; losing this deal has strategic GTM impact.

Request: Markus/Laura — please advise which option to accept or whether we should offer a hybrid (e.g., 30% + net-45 + 60-day reconciliation). If we need to accept Option C, we should request a short-term SLA credit and a limited indemnity carve-out.

I'll schedule a 30-min exec decision call if helpful; DocuSign link for their countersign is ready (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abcdef123456).

—Naomi
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
